newsitem.title: EGYPT: Europe says wants action to support Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Europe says wants action to support Mideast peace.

text.p: Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring told Egyptian counterpart Amr Moussa on Monday Europe wanted "concrete" results from Palestinian-Israeli peace talks to help keep the Middle East peace process on track.

Spring, in Cairo before heading for Israel to meet Palestinian and Israeli officials, told reporters Europe was also willing to offer financial and political help to support Palestinian-Israeli peace accords.

"We have reaffirmed our desire to offer assistance to the peace process and also our desire that concise and concrete steps are taken (by Palestinians and Israelis) to show the world that the peace process is on the right track," Spring said.
"Europe is very worried at not having a force in the region to push the peace process," Spring said. "We are watching the situation closely."

Frustrated at its exclusion from the U.S.-brokered peace talks, the European Union decided on Saturday to send Spring to the region. The 15-nation bloc also said it would appoint a special envoy to help in the peace talks.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiatiors met on Monday to discuss the long delayed Israeli troop withdrawal from Hebron -- the last of seven towns to be given to Palestinian self-rule -- and other peace pledges put on hold since hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was elected in May.

Netanyahu, who angered the Palestinians, Arabs and Europe by saying he wanted to alter a 1993 peace deal to secure Jewish settlers living in Hebron, told parliament on Monday he would stick to the troop withdrawal as stipulated by the accord.
But he did not give a date or details of the security arrangements his negotiators were wrangling out with the Palestinians.

U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher has pressured Israel into honouring the troop pull-back but the United States's role in the region has traditionally been seen by many Arabs as tilted towards the Jewish state.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat stopped in both France and Italy on his way home from an emergency meeting with Netanyahu in Washington to ask for a European presence in talks with the Jewish state.
Moussa said Egypt, host of several rounds of peace negotiations, also welcomed the EU's involvement as "additional support" to the American and Egyptian role.

"This will support the American and Egyptian involvement in the peace process, particularly as the European role is known for its clarity and a position based on the (1991) Madrid and (1993) Oslo peace accords," the Egyptian minister added.
Egypt has said the region would be thrown into crisis if Israel did not change its hardline stance in the the current Palestinian-Israeli negotiations.
Spring will also meet Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak at the northeastern town of Ismailiya where the Egyptian leader will watch a naval parade marking Egypt's 1973 war with Israel.
Arafat will also meet Mubarak in Ismailiya to brief him on Sunday's round of talks on Hebron. It was not immediately clear whether Spring and Arafat will also meet there.
